# Transition atlas

<!-- Generated by tools/build_transitions.py from docs/transitions/data.json. Edit the JSON, then rerun. -->

**Live page with looping demos: [https://tugrawork-creator.github.io/saas-motion-kit/transitions/](https://tugrawork-creator.github.io/saas-motion-kit/transitions/)**

HyperFrames already ships the stock transitions (crossfade, blur crossfade, push, zoom-through, circle iris, blinds and the shader set).
A good film repeats two or three of those as its rhythm. This atlas holds the other kind: 24 **narrative transitions** that carry meaning from one scene into the next.

How to use it:

1. **Keep a quiet base.** Plain hard cuts can carry the in-between beats. Log them as `motif:cut` in the ledger so the audit knows they are deliberate, and never let a flashy transition become the default.
2. **Spend narrative ones where the story turns:** the hook, the reveal, the proof moment, the CTA. Pick the one whose meaning matches that cut.
3. **Never twice.** Use each atlas transition once per film, and don't put two from the same family back to back.

Energy runs from ●○○ (calm) to ●●● (high). Tones use a fixed vocabulary: bold, calm, celebratory, mysterious, nostalgic, playful, premium, technical, trustworthy, urgent, warm.
Every entry in `data.json` also has a one-line description and a seek-safe GSAP recipe (transform, opacity, clip-path and filter only, explicit `fromTo`).

## Cut

The edit does the work. No overlap and no wipe: the match between the last frame of A and the first frame of B carries the meaning.

| Name | Energy | Tones | When | Avoid | HyperFrames |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **T01 Match Cut: Shape** | ●○○ | premium, calm, trustworthy | Reframing a problem as its answer: the coral alert dot becomes the teal status ring. Best on the hook-to-reveal cut, where the viewer should feel 'same thing, new meaning'. | A near-miss in position or size reads as a mistake, so lock both shapes to one centre. Use it once per film; a second shape match turns a clever beat into a gimmick. | custom (hard cut); css-other morph circle is the nearest built-in |
| **T02 Match Cut: Motion** | ●●○ | bold, playful, premium | Handing momentum from cause to effect: a 'Deploy' pill slides right and a 'Shipped' badge lands where it was heading. Good for workflow steps that should feel like one gesture. | Direction, screen position and speed must match on the cut frame or the eye jumps. Don't cut on a still object, and don't follow it with a whip pan: two directional handoffs in a row blur together. | custom (hard cut); css-blur directional blur can soften the seam |
| **T03 Graphic Match: Color** | ●●○ | bold, premium, warm | Going from a detail to a chapter card or brand moment: the teal bar in a chart becomes the teal of the next scene, so the colour carries the idea ('growth') across. | Needs a flat, clean colour area; gradients, photos and textures break the match. Pointless between two scenes that already share a background. | css-other (morph circle), closest; here the colour comes from a push-in, not a circle |
| **T04 Beat Cut with Hold-frame** | ●●● | urgent, bold, celebratory | The 'wait for it' before a reveal or a drop: the freeze tells the viewer to look, the downbeat cut delivers the answer. Built for music-led promos and launch reels. | Only on a real downbeat; off the grid it reads as a glitch. One hold per section at most, and never on a frame the viewer still needs to read. | custom (hard cut on the beat grid) |

## Carry

Something survives the change. An object, a word, a cursor or a line walks from one scene into the next and becomes part of it.

| Name | Energy | Tones | When | Avoid | HyperFrames |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **T05 Object Carry** | ●●○ | playful, trustworthy, warm | Showing one item moving through a system: an alert becomes a ticket, a file becomes a row, a card lands on a board. The viewer follows the object, so the scene change feels earned. | The object needs an obvious destination in B. One carried object per transition, and not on the next cut too: carry after carry starts to feel like a screensaver. | shared-element (Tier-A, worker-authored) |
| **T06 Type Carry** | ●○○ | calm, premium, trustworthy | When the next scene proves one word of the claim: 'watched' becomes the title of the monitoring panel, 'owned' becomes the owner column. A calm bridge from headline to proof. | The word must mean the same thing in both scenes. Don't carry filler words, don't swap the font mid-flight, and don't carry type twice in a row. | shared-element (Tier-A, worker-authored) |
| **T07 Cursor Carry** | ●●○ | technical, trustworthy, calm | Product demos and walkthroughs: 'click here and this opens'. Cause and effect are on screen, so it suits navigation and drilling into detail. | The clicked element must be what the next scene is about. Keep the cursor slow and deliberate; don't click into a screen with no clear target, or three times in one demo. | shared-element (Tier-A); rules card-morph-anchor + cursor-click-ripple |
| **T08 Line-to-Horizon** | ●○○ | calm, warm, premium | Going from data to meaning: 'the numbers settled' becomes a calm landscape, a roadmap or a section divider. Good for the exhale after a proof moment. | Needs one clean line, not a busy multi-series chart, and a scene B with a strong horizontal. Don't reuse it for the outro. | custom |

## Camera

Move the lens, not the layers. Push through, whip, pull back or slide in depth, so the viewer travels between scenes.

| Name | Energy | Tones | When | Avoid | HyperFrames |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **T09 Push-Through** | ●●● | bold, technical, mysterious | Going deeper: from the dashboard into one report, from the overview into the product. Works as a hero reveal because it feels like entering the product. | The window must hold a true miniature of B, or the landing jumps. It is high energy: once per film, and not straight after a zoom or dolly. | css-scale (zoom through), aimed at a UI window |
| **T10 Whip Pan with Motion Blur** | ●●● | urgent, playful, bold | Two things happening at once ('meanwhile, in support…') or a quick before/after. Adds energy without changing the subject. | Twice per film at most, and never back and forth in a row. Only a horizontal blur sells it; a plain gaussian blur reads as a focus problem. | shader: whip pan · css-blur (directional blur) |
| **T11 Dolly-Out Reveal** | ●●○ | premium, trustworthy, celebratory | Revealing scale or context: 'this is one of 40 workflows', 'every team gets this view'. A strong move from one feature to the whole platform. | The other tiles must be real, readable product surfaces, not filler. Don't follow it with a push into a different tile; it reads as indecision. | css-scale (zoom out), inverted into a grid |
| **T12 Parallax Slide** | ●●○ | warm, playful, calm | Stepping through a sequence (plan, build, ship) when a plain push feels flat. The depth turns a sideways move into travel through a space. | Three layers with clear ratios (about 0.3×, 1×, 1.4×) and no more. Not for dense data scenes: text moving at different speeds is hard to read. | css-push (push slide), split into three depth layers |

## Mask

One scene opens a window onto the next. The window's shape is the message: the logo, a word, the subject, a strip.

| Name | Energy | Tones | When | Avoid | HyperFrames |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **T13 Product-Shape Mask** | ●●○ | premium, bold, celebratory | Brand-to-product moments: the logo opens onto the product, the app icon opens onto the app. Also a strong first cut after a cold open. | The shape must be recognisable when small, so use simple marks and UI shapes. Once per film, and not in the same film as a text mask. | css-radial (circle / diamond iris) with a custom clip shape; shader: sdf-iris |
| **T14 Text Mask** | ●●○ | bold, premium, mysterious | Title moments and chapter openers where one word is the message ('LIVE', 'NOW', the product name). The classic name reveal for a launch film. | Needs heavy type and a visually rich scene B, or the letters look empty. Short words only (3–5 letters); never twice per film. | custom (mix-blend knockout) |
| **T15 Focal Iris** | ●●○ | technical, urgent, mysterious | Drilling into a detail: 'look here, and this is what it means'. Where the iris starts tells the viewer what caused the next scene. | Make the subject obvious first (pulse or ring it). Don't open from the centre (that's the stock iris) or on a busy frame with two possible subjects. | css-radial (circle iris) with the origin moved to the subject |
| **T16 Split Stack** | ●●● | bold, technical, urgent | Topic changes and list beats ('three things changed'): the strips feel editorial and structured. Also good in a fast feature montage. | Line the strips up with B's layout so no headline is cut in half at rest. Too busy for calm films; don't pair it with other stripe or blind effects. | css-cover (staggered blocks / blinds), reduced to three strips |

## Material

The frame is made of something. Paper folds, ink bleeds, pixels sort and glass bends: a tactile handoff.

| Name | Energy | Tones | When | Avoid | HyperFrames |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **T17 Paper Fold** | ●○○ | warm, playful, nostalgic | Closing one chapter and opening the next: a report folded into a proposal, a draft put away. Friendly and analogue, good for onboarding and small-team stories. | Needs a perspective parent, and the front and back faces must swap at exactly 90° or the fold flickers. Too slow for launch energy; never fold twice in a film. | css-3d (3D card flip), closest |
| **T18 Ink Bleed** | ●○○ | mysterious, premium, warm | Moments of commitment and craft: signing, approving, publishing. Feels handmade, a welcome contrast in a very digital film. | Needs a slow, calm track; fast ink looks like a paint splash. One ink colour only, and not in the same film as glitch or dither. | shader: domain warp / cross-warp morph, closest |
| **T19 Dither / Pixel Sort** | ●●● | technical, nostalgic, bold | Tech moments: data being processed, an AI 'thinking', a system rebuilding. A retro-digital accent that suits developer tools. | Chunky pixels only; fine dither vanishes in video compression. Once per film, and never over small text that must stay readable. | css-grid (grid dissolve), closest; shader: glitch |
| **T20 Glass Refraction Wipe** | ●○○ | premium, calm, technical | Premium, calm reveals: a new plan, a redesigned screen, a before/after told with restraint. | backdrop-filter is heavy to render, so keep the pane narrow and the move short. It doesn't read on flat, empty scenes; don't combine it with other blur transitions. | custom; shader: chromatic split for the fringe |

## Time

Bend the clock. Freeze, rewind, ramp or tick through time, so the transition itself says 'earlier', 'later' or 'again'.

| Name | Energy | Tones | When | Avoid | HyperFrames |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **T21 Freeze & Rewind Scrub** | ●●○ | nostalgic, playful, technical | Root-cause stories ('let's go back to 09:42'), flashbacks and 'how did we get here' openers. | The rewind has to reverse motion the viewer just saw, or it looks like a random glitch. Once per film; skip the VHS noise for a premium brand. | css-distortion (VHS tape) for the rewind texture |
| **T22 Speed Ramp** | ●●● | urgent, bold, celebratory | Covering distance or time in one breath: 'from plan to launch', flying along a roadmap, the drop in the music. | Needs continuous motion on both sides to ramp. One or two per film, on the biggest musical moments, and not next to a whip pan. | css-blur (blur through / directional blur) at the peak |
| **T23 Time-lapse Tick** | ●●○ | trustworthy, warm, nostalgic | Results over time: 'a week later', 'by Friday', a sprint in five seconds. Time itself becomes the proof. | The content must change as time passes, not just the clock. It implies waiting, so not for instant results; don't pair it with a speed ramp. | css-mechanical (clock wipe), closest |
| **T24 Loop Seam** | ●○○ | calm, premium, playful | Booth screens, social loops, website hero videos and GIFs: anything that plays on repeat, often without sound. | Every property must match at the seam: position, colour, grain, even a particle's phase. Don't hide a bad seam with a fade; it shows on every loop. | custom; verify with tools/loop_check.py |
